what_its_for: Bosentan is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the arteries that carry blood to your lungs. It helps relax and widen these blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, making it easier for you to breathe and exercise.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Take it at the same times each day, usually in the morning and evening. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets unless your doctor specifically tells you to. If you have trouble swallowing the tablet, ask your doctor or pharmacist about other options.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a lower dose of 62.5 mg twice a day for the first 4 weeks. After that, your dose will likely be increased to 125 mg twice a day. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on how you respond to the medication and your liver test results. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store bosentan at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about safe disposal options.
what_to_avoid: Do not take bosentan if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant — it can cause serious birth defects. You must use two reliable forms of birth control while taking this medication. Avoid glyburide (a diabetes medicine) as the combination can cause liver problems. Do not drink grapefruit juice, as it may affect how your body processes this drug. Avoid starting any new prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medicines — especially St. John's Wort — without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many drugs can interact with bosentan.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, unusual tiredness or weakness, severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting — these may be signs of liver problems. Also call your doctor if you experience swelling in your legs or ankles, unexplained weight gain, shortness of breath that gets worse, or if you think you may be pregnant. You will need regular blood tests (usually every month) to check your liver and blood counts, so keep all your lab and doctor appointments.
when_it_works: Bosentan starts working within a few days, but you may not notice the full benefit for several weeks. Most patients begin to feel improvements in their ability to exercise and breathe more easily within 4 to 12 weeks of starting treatment. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well, as stopping suddenly can make your condition worse.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Bosentan must NOT be used during pregnancy. It causes serious birth defects. Women who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting, every month during treatment, and one month after stopping. Two reliable forms of birth control are required throughout treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking bosentan. Children: Bosentan can be used in children, but the dose is based on weight and determined by a specialist. Liver disease: This medication is generally not recommended if you already have moderate to severe liver problems, as it can make liver disease worse. Elderly patients: Older adults can use bosentan, but should be monitored closely for side effects.
